newsitem.title: FRANCE: LVMH stock rockets on DFS deal.
newsitem.headline: LVMH stock rockets on DFS deal.

text.p: Shares in luxury goods group LVMH rocketed on the Paris bourse on Wednesday after an arbitrator cleared LVMH's bid to acquire U.S. duty free chain DFS.

LVMH said in a statement on Wednesday that the planned acquisition of DFS, which now hinges only on U.S. regulatory approval, would boost its operating profit by around 30 percent and turnover by close to 50 percent.
LVMH's stock was up 4.59 percent at 1,300 francs at 1000 GMT. The bourse's CAC-40 index was up 0.6 percent.
The arbitrator's decision, announced on Tuesday, resolved a quarrel among DFS shareholders over the deal announced in October.
"The statements by LVMH about the purchase are pretty good for the company," said one dealer. "The fact that the arbitrator has given approval lifts uncertainty about the deal."

LVMH said DFS's financial performance was exceptional -- it has an operating margin close to 15 percent, average return on equity of 85 percent in the past three years and cash flow averaging $290 million annually over the past three years.
"The world's leading luxury goods group thus acquires the world's leading retailer of luxury goods," LVMH said in the statement.
